clue.text: Deliveries in security container get some press reporting

indicators.note: the deliveries are set inside the security container, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a cage is a container that keeps something secure
in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries

explanation.surface: Something delivered in a locked container attracts the attention of the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliveries' points to cricket: an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end, and 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Coverage is the amount of attention newspapers give a story, i.e. their reporting of it.

clue.text: Cost of cleaner, say, going up

parts.note: a char or charwoman is a British name for a cleaning lady

indicators.note: in a down light, going up means reading the piece from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated e.g.

explanation.surface: The price of hiring a cleaner, for instance, is rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' signals the reversal in this down light. A char is an old British word for a cleaning woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge is the price asked for a service, its cost.

clue.text: Subject to restriction over balance of words

indicators.note: the following word is restricted, cut short by losing its opening letter

parts.note: BAL is the abbreviation for balance on a bank statement

explanation.surface: Words are weighed and limited in some sort of trade-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject to restriction' trims OVER to VER; 'over' is not a reversal signal here but the word being cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbal means relating to or expressed in words.

clue.text: Prepare to travel again on deck

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters
a pack of cards is also called a deck

explanation.surface: A passenger readies luggage once more while standing on a ship's deck.
explanation.definitionFit: To repack is to fill a suitcase once more, readying for another journey.

clue.text: Bird lacking experience fell outside hospital

parts.note: a green recruit is inexperienced

indicators.note: the word for fell goes round the outside of the hospital letter

parts.note: to fall is to sink, so fell is sank
H is the abbreviation for hospital on maps and signs

explanation.surface: A novice birdwatcher collapsed outside a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts SANK around H.
explanation.definitionFit: The greenshank is a wading bird with long greenish legs.

clue.text: Piece left over -bad economy

parts.note: food that has gone off has gone bad
a cut is a saving or economy in spending

explanation.surface: A leftover scrap, and a complaint that making cuts is poor economy.
explanation.definitionFit: An offcut is a scrap of material remaining after the main piece is trimmed.

clue.text: Sheep on a path taking little space up

parts.note: a fold is a flock of sheep, or their pen
a way is a path or road

explanation.surface: Sheep walking a path climb a short way upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Foldaway furniture collapses for storage, so occupies little room.

clue.text: Cryptic designation for Caedmon, possibly English

indicators.note: possibly suggests the name could be some other arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A secret title for Caedmon, the first named English poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges CAEDMON. Caedmon was a seventh-century Anglo-Saxon poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A code name is a secret label used to conceal what is being referred to.

clue.text: Crowd work regularly at wool

parts.note: from the saying two's company, three's a crowd
to ply a trade is to work at it steadily

explanation.surface: A mass of people steadily working at wool.
explanation.walkthrough: THREE comes from the proverb 'two's company, three's a crowd'.
explanation.definitionFit: Three-ply is yarn made of three twisted strands, a kind of knitting wool.

clue.text: Rate of movement of Concorde from Paris, flying by river flowing east

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters of the city's name are sent about into a new order
the river's name runs the other way from its usual reading in this across light

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland, and another in Wales and England

explanation.surface: How fast Concorde goes after taking off from Paris, passing over a river heading eastwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges the French capital's letters, and 'flowing east' runs the Dee backwards; 'Concorde' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Airspeed is an aircraft's velocity relative to the air, its rate of movement in flight.

clue.text: Fuel-saving transport top in Germany

indicators.note: the top is placed within the abbreviation for Germany

parts.note: a lid is the top of a container

explanation.surface: A plea for economical vehicles that lead the way in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' is not a first-letter signal here but a lid, set 'in' the abbreviation for Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: A glider is an aircraft flying without an engine, so it uses no fuel at all.

clue.text: Looking to find good school

parts.note: Lancing College is an English private school in West Sussex

explanation.surface: Someone is searching for a good school.
explanation.walkthrough: LANCING is Lancing College, a well-known English boarding school on the Sussex coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Glancing is looking briefly, taking a quick look at something.

clue.text: In which you could have gutted sardine mashed up?

definitions.text: In which you could have gutted sardine mashed up?

indicators.note: fish that is mashed up is pulped and its parts jumbled, so the letters are rearranged
a gutted fish has had its insides removed, here the D from the centre of the word

explanation.surface: A question about which snack might hold a sardine that has been cleaned and mashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' removes the central D from SARDINE, leaving SARINE; 'mashed up' rearranges that. SARNIE is British slang for a sandwich, and mashed sardine is a classic filling.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandwich is the snack into which a mashed sardine filling could be put.

clue.text: Woman's given authority without job

parts.note: Una is a woman's name; with the possessive it gives UNAS
a document signed off has been given authority

explanation.surface: A woman has been given power although she has no actual post.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unassigned has not been allotted any task or post.

clue.text: Ghostly place, home to

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Ghostly place, home to (10)' is cut short: 'Ghostly' defines it and P (place) may start it, but the words giving the rest of the letters are missing and no print or search supplies them.

clue.text: After taking dole I leave with yen for getting everywhere

parts.note: UB stands for unemployment benefit, the dole
to quit is to leave
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: After collecting benefit, someone goes off longing to travel all over.
explanation.walkthrough: UB, unemployment benefit, is the British dole money.
explanation.definitionFit: Ubiquity is the quality of being present everywhere at once.

clue.text: Fiesta made secure by this process?

definitions.text: Fiesta made secure by this process?

parts.words: Fiesta made secure by this process?
parts.note: Fiesta is a small Ford car model, kept safe by being put away in a shelter at home

explanation.surface: A festival is protected by some procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiesta' looks like a party but is the Ford Fiesta, a popular small car.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting a car in its shed at night protects it from theft and weather.

clue.text: Means of forcing one male Lord to accommodate two Liberals

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the lord takes in, or houses, the two Liberals within his own letters

parts.note: a lord is a peer of the realm
L is the abbreviation for Liberal, so two of them give LL

explanation.surface: A man is pressed into service by a nobleman putting up two Liberal politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accommodate' signals the lord housing the Liberals; 'Means of forcing' is a device, not a method.
explanation.definitionFit: An impeller is a rotor in a pump that drives fluid along, a device for forcing it.

clue.text: Eastern religion given support by monarch in doctrine

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
HM stands for His or Her Majesty, a monarch
a doctrine is an ism, written here as the two words an ism

explanation.surface: A faith in the East is upheld by the king as part of official teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctrine' gives AN ISM, a doctrine being an ism; 'given support by' puts BRA in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Brahmanism is the early form of Hinduism centred on the priestly Brahmin class, an Eastern faith.

clue.text: Popular company's not healthy

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a firm is a business company

explanation.surface: A popular business is ailing.
explanation.definitionFit: Infirm means weak or sickly, lacking good health.

clue.text: Pigment, one found in purgative drug

indicators.note: the single letter is discovered inside the name of the drug

parts.note: senna is a plant-based laxative
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A colouring agent is discovered within a laxative medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts I inside SENNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is an earth used as a brownish-yellow pigment by painters.

clue.text: Get ready to fly giving fellow support

parts.note: a ledge is a shelf that supports things

explanation.surface: A person preparing to take off is given a helping hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To fledge is for a young bird to grow its feathers, readying it for flight.

clue.text: Note Queen's at head of state

indicators.note: the queen piece comes at the top of the word for state, in front of it

parts.note: QU is a dictionary abbreviation for queen
to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: A remark that the Queen leads the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: QU is a less common abbreviation for queen than the usual Q or R.
explanation.definitionFit: A quaver is a musical note, an eighth note, half the length of a crotchet.

clue.text: Alien in Britain, initially up for review at two-year intervals

indicators.note: initially means take only the first letter of the following word
something up for review is to be reconsidered and reworked, so the letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: A foreigner living in Britain finds that permission to stay is reconsidered every couple of years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives B from Britain; 'up for review' rearranges ALIEN IN plus B.
explanation.definitionFit: Biennial means happening once every second year.

clue.text: It depends on the weather being cold

definitions.text: It depends on the weather being cold

parts.words: It depends on the weather being cold
parts.note: depends is read literally as hangs down: a thing that dangles from eaves only when the weather is freezing

explanation.surface: A shrug that the outcome depends on whether it turns cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depends' looks like 'is conditional on' but is used in its old sense of 'hangs down'.
explanation.definitionFit: An icicle is a hanging spike of frozen water, formed only in freezing weather.

clue.text: Far from secured, such a cash card would be useless

definitions.text: such a cash card would be useless

explanation.surface: A card that is not fastened down, and a bank card without its code being of no use.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the word as un-PIN-ned: a cash card with no personal identification number cannot be used.
explanation.definitionFit: Not fastened by a pin means loose; a card lacking its personal identification number cannot work at a cash machine.

clue.text: Dairy product offered by innovative guy to first of restaurateurs

indicators.note: an innovative person makes something new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement
first of means take only the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: An inventive man supplies a milk-based food to leading restaurant owners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first of' gives R from restaurateurs; 'innovative' rearranges GUY TO plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: Yogurt is fermented milk, a dairy food.

clue.text: A female's vending water

parts.note: a dam is a mother animal, a female parent
vending is selling, a sale

explanation.surface: A woman is selling bottled water.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam's ale is a jocular old name for plain water, the only drink of the first man.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's ale is an old humorous phrase for drinking water.
